assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Vicsek flocking model, the Toner-Tu hydrodynamic theory of polar flocks and the Ramaswamy-type hydrodynamics of active fluids established active matter as a coherent branch of nonequilibrium statistical physics. Long-range order in two dimensions in violation of the Mermin-Wagner expectation, giant number fluctuations and new universality classes are conceptually original and clear, and the ideas reach bird flocks, bacterial suspensions, cytoskeletal gels and synthetic swimmers.
assessment.attribution: Vicsek supplied the minimal numerical model, Toner and Tu the continuum theory and the renormalisation-group argument for order, and Ramaswamy the hydrodynamics of active suspensions and the number-fluctuation results. The three-person configuration is natural; Tu and others are not in the credited names, which leaves some theory credit outside the prize.
assessment.maturity: Core predictions have been tested in experiments on vibrated granular matter, colloidal rollers, bacterial turbulence and cell monolayers, and the theory has been stable for about three decades. Timing is good, though experimental verification of some exact exponents is still partial.
uncertainties: Quantitative confirmation of the Toner-Tu exponents in real systems is incomplete.
Credit for the continuum theory is shared with people not among the credited names (for example Yuhai Tu).
Whether the committee views active matter as a unified discovery or a field of applications is a judgement.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at magic twist angles and the 2018 observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum matter, a new tunable platform for strongly correlated and topological physics with a very large and fast-growing literature.
assessment.attribution: The theory by Bistritzer and MacDonald and the decisive experiments by Jarillo-Herrero and collaborators form a clean theory plus experiment pairing. I would propose Jarillo-Herrero and MacDonald, with Bistritzer's role as co-author of the key calculation noted; the first-author experimental credit (Yuan Cao) and other contributors fall outside the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced by many groups and extended to many moire systems; the field is young and the microscopic origin of superconductivity is still debated, so the maturity is good for the discovery but not for the full interpretation.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism for superconductivity remains unsettled.
Possible tension between a prize for the discovery and the unfinished understanding.
Earlier theory on twisted bilayers (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto; Suarez Morell et al.) may deserve consideration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, predicted by Kane and Mele and observed in HgTe quantum wells by Molenkamp's group, introduced a new classification of band insulators with protected edge states. This is a fundamental, original and clearly established concept with broad influence on materials physics and topological matter.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical breakthrough; Molenkamp led the first experimental realisation. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed the HgTe route and are not in the credited names, which complicates a fair configuration, and the three-dimensional topological insulators (Fu, Kane, Mele; Moore, Balents; Hasan) are a separate credit stream.
assessment.maturity: Very well confirmed by transport and ARPES; the work is more than fifteen years old and widely taught. Recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: The omitted HgTe proposal (Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang) is a credit question.
The relation of this candidate to the overlapping B010 and B035 entries involves a choice of how to define the prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organising principle of the cell, shown with P granules and nucleoli, links soft-matter and statistical physics to cell biology and provides quantitative physical descriptions of intracellular organisation. Originality and impact are high, and from a complex-systems viewpoint the use of phase-separation theory in a living system is attractive.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne made the decisive experimental discovery in 2009; Jülicher contributed the theoretical framework for active droplets and non-equilibrium condensates. This is a plausible three-person split, but the physics-versus-biology boundary makes it a delicate fit for the physics prize.
assessment.maturity: Rapid adoption, though many claims of condensate function in vivo are debated and the role of phase separation versus other assembly mechanisms is contested in specific cases.
uncertainties: Disciplinary fit with the physics prize is uncertain.
Debate over which cellular structures truly are liquid-like condensates.
Other contributors to the physical theory (for example Rosen, Michael Rosen's group) are outside the credited list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise Hubbard-type many-body models with tunable parameters, with the observation of the superfluid-Mott transition and later quantum gas microscopes. The concept of analogue quantum simulation links atomic physics to condensed-matter theory and is important and original.
assessment.attribution: Zoller and Cirac (with Jaksch and others) made the theoretical proposals, while Greiner and Bloch carried out the Mott-insulator observation and developed the microscopes. The configuration is hard because the credited names comprise two theorists and two experimentalists, and four people exceed the limit of three.
assessment.maturity: Mature and broadly confirmed; the field has been recognised in part by the 2001 and 2012 prizes (BEC; control of quantum systems), which may argue against another atomic-physics prize.
uncertainties: Overlap with prior prizes in cold-atom physics.
Exclusion of Cirac or Jaksch in a three-person selection is difficult to justify.
Whether the simulators have solved problems beyond classical computation is still being debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory, exact in infinite dimensions, is the standard non-perturbative framework for strongly correlated electrons and led to a quantitative description of the Mott transition and, combined with ab initio methods, of correlated materials. It is a conceptually elegant theory used widely.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt introduced the infinite-dimension limit, Georges and Kotliar built the mapping onto the Anderson impurity model, with Müller-Hartmann and Jarrell also central. The attribution is crowded and a three-person prize would leave out significant contributors.
assessment.maturity: Mature, widely used for decades; confirmation is by comparison with experiment and numerical benchmarks, with limits at low dimension and in treating non-local correlations.
uncertainties: Credit shared with Metzner, Müller-Hartmann and others who are not in the credited names.
Approximate in finite dimensions, so the predictive status is method-dependent.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Fluctuation theorems, including the Evans-Searles, Gallavotti-Cohen and Jarzynski relations, give exact statements about work and entropy production far from equilibrium and are now the basis of stochastic thermodynamics. It is a foundational result in statistical physics that I find important and conceptually clean.
assessment.attribution: Jarzynski, Evans and Gallavotti are credible choices, but Cohen, Crooks, Searles and Morriss also have claims, so any three-person set leaves substantial credit unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally verified in single-molecule pulling, colloids and small circuits; now standard in teaching. Timing is acceptable, though influence on technology is limited.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among several close contributors is unresolved.
Experimental impact is concentrated in small systems and is less far-reaching than other candidates.
Not a single discovery but a family of related results.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics, with strong coupling of superconducting qubits to microwave resonators, is the architecture behind much of present superconducting quantum computing and provides a clean platform for light-matter physics.
assessment.attribution: Blais and collaborators provided the theory proposal, and Wallraff and Schoelkopf led the first strong-coupling experiments. The configuration is reasonable but overlaps with the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits and with other quantum-computing credit.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many groups and widely deployed; technological relevance is high, though the timing relative to the recent 2025 prize on superconducting circuits is a consideration.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 superconducting-circuit prize.
Hardware and engineering contributions beyond the credited names are significant.
